title: Add Latency/$ benchmark report landing page + FAQ + methodology appendix
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs/website: Adds a public landing page for the Latency/$ Benchmark Report with FAQ and methodology appendix; includes disclosure language and versioning hooks for future refreshes.
description:
Summary: Adds the public-facing benchmark report landing page to the docs/marketing site, including (1) core narrative + CTAs, (2) an FAQ tuned for engineering + procurement questions, and (3) a methodology appendix that mirrors internal guidance while staying publish-safe. This PR intentionally avoids hard “we’re #1” claims and instead emphasizes reproducibility, constraints, and how to interpret results.

Context / why: We need a single canonical URL we can link from the blog post, lifecycle emails, and field enablement. The page should (a) explain “latency per dollar” in plain terms, (b) provide enough methodology detail to be credible, and (c) answer the predictable objections (variance, caching, region differences, workload mismatch) without burying the lead. This PR is the web surface; charts/data tables will be wired in via the existing build pipeline in follow-up work.

What’s included: Landing page at /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar with hero + explainer sections, CTAs (download PDF, view methodology, contact sales), and an SEO-friendly FAQ. Methodology appendix at /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology with explicit definitions (workloads, concurrency, warmup policy, what’s included in cost, and how we compute latency/$). FAQ entries covering: what latency/$ is, how to map results to my workload, what regions are covered, how caching/batching affects results, what variance to expect, what we do to avoid benchmark-only tuning, and how to reproduce a smaller-scale run. Disclosure language and constraints: highlights that results depend on workload shape, sequence lengths, concurrency, and regional capacity conditions; emphasizes confidence intervals / rerun policy at a high level. Internal hooks for refresh cadence: page includes a “Results version” slot (date + commit hash placeholder) and a “Last updated” banner element.

Not included / out of scope: No raw per-request logs; no customer data; no competitor callouts; no absolute superiority statements. Public tables/charts are referenced as placeholders (components exist but not yet hooked to final artifacts).

Implementation details: Uses existing docs site layout components with a new Benchmarks template variant (hero + sticky TOC on desktop). Adds FAQ schema markup (JSON-LD) for SEO; FAQ answers are written to pass legal review (no unqualified superlatives). CTAs include UTM placeholders; actual UTMs will be configured by Marketing Ops at publish time. Methodology appendix includes a “Definitions” section to disambiguate latency vs TTFT vs per-token latency; we keep TTFT wording conservative until final chart set is locked.

Files / areas changed (high level): apps/docs/src/pages/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar.mdx (new landing page content + sections + CTAs) apps/docs/src/pages/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology.mdx (new methodology appendix) apps/docs/src/components/benchmarks/BenchmarkHero.tsx (new hero variant for report pages) apps/docs/src/components/benchmarks/BenchmarkFAQ.tsx (FAQ component + schema markup) apps/docs/src/components/benchmarks/DisclosureCallout.tsx (new callout for constraints/disclosures) apps/docs/src/styles/benchmarks.css (minor layout + accessibility tweaks; contrast checked) apps/docs/src/content/seo/benchmarks-latency-per-dollar.ts (title/description/canonical config) apps/docs/src/routes.ts (adds page routes)

Copy notes (what we optimized for): A page that engineers trust: concrete definitions, the “what’s included” list, and explicit caveats about workload matching. A page that procurement understands: positioning latency/$ as a unit economics metric and clarifying what is and isn’t in the cost denominator. Consistency with claims guidelines: avoids “best/fastest/cheapest” without qualifiers; uses “measured under the methodology described below” consistently.

Screenshots: Added preview screenshots in the PR comments (desktop + mobile). Sticky TOC on methodology page is confirmed to not overlap with the header.

Test plan: yarn test (unit) yarn lint yarn build && preview the two new routes locally Check links: landing page -> methodology, PDF download stub, contact CTAs Validate JSON-LD output for FAQ in page source

Commits: docs: add latency/$ landing page scaffold docs: add methodology appendix + definitions docs: add FAQ + JSON-LD schema markup design: add disclosure callout component chore: wire routes + SEO metadata

Review notes / discussion highlights: Soojin Lee: Requested tightening the hero copy to lead with “production economics” vs “benchmarks” and to avoid implying universal generality; applied. Also asked to move “Download PDF” CTA below the first explanatory paragraph to reduce bounce on mobile; applied. Wei Chen: Flagged that our initial FAQ answer implied the public table includes p99 and “per-request logs”; corrected to “aggregated percentiles” and removed any hint of log publication. Also asked to add a short “How to reproduce” section that points to the example repo (without promising exact parity); added as a final FAQ entry + callout. Jonas Weber: Requested that methodology clarifies the warmup window and caching policy in plain terms, and that we explicitly define whether cost uses list price vs effective fleet cost; updated to say “public pricing inputs” and “metered usage” language (kept non-sensitive). Also suggested adding the phrase “confidence bands / variance summaries are included in the report” rather than “confidence intervals” (since format may be bands); applied. Tessa Morgan: Requested small accessibility tweaks: ensure chart placeholder colors meet contrast; added CSS + adjusted callout background. Also asked for consistent spacing between sections and a max-width tweak for long FAQ answers; applied. Michael Grant (Legal): Requested adding a disclosure line near the top: “This report reflects measurements conducted by Redwood Inference; results will vary by workload and environment.” Also asked to remove “industry-leading” from one section and replace with “production-grade”; applied.

CI: buildkite/redwood-docs:lint (pass) buildkite/redwood-docs:test (pass) buildkite/redwood-docs:build (pass) lighthouse-ci (pass; accessibility 97, SEO 100, perf 93 on preview)

Merge plan: Squash merge after copy + legal sign-off. Follow-up PR will connect final charts/data artifacts and update the “Results version” placeholders once the public table generator is finalized.

Checklist: [x] Copy reviewed by Marketing (Soojin) [x] Methodology reviewed by Applied ML (Jonas) [x] Legal review completed (Michael) [x] Accessibility basics checked (contrast, headings, focus) [x] Links validated
